rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing - sale or licensing of algorithmic devices
rules.requirement: The proposed ordinance would make it unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord. An algorithmic device is software or a product that uses algorithms to perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend to a landlord rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.coverage_text: Any person who sells, licenses, or otherwise provides an algorithmic device to a landlord; algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Algorithmic device does not include software or a product used to publish reports on rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or from information available to the general public, that does not recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for future leases or renewals; or software or a product used to establish rental rates or income limits in accordance with local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.quoted_span: (a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This Ordinance will take effect and be in force on the thirtieth day from and after its final passage.

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing - landlord use of algorithmic devices
rules.requirement: The proposed ordinance would make it unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. Each month a violation exists or continues, and each residential rental property for which a landlord uses an algorithmic device, is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property in the City of San Diego using algorithmic devices that perform calculations of nonpublic competitor data to set rental rates or occupancy levels.
rules.exemptions: Algorithmic device does not include software or a product used to publish reports on rental rates or occupancy levels from aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or from information available to the general public, that does not recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for future leases or renewals; or software or a product used to establish rental rates or income limits in accordance with local, state, or federal affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.penalty: A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation in a civil action against a landlord; a prevailing tenant shall recover costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: (b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This Ordinance will take effect and be in force on the thirtieth day from and after its final passage.
rules.interaction_text: The remedies under section 98.1104 are cumulative and are in addition to any other remedies in this Division or at law, statute, or ordinance.
